decisions.reason: As a close-to-core cardboard quarter-pallet variant, it is inexpensive for a large display producer to keep as an option while customer demand is still being learned.
The pegboard-back format is still well within the firm’s core display capabilities, so the option value of staying in the market likely exceeds the low cost of keeping it available.
This standard cardboard quarter-pallet display fits the firm’s main business and can be retained while management observes whether it wins repeat orders against nearby variants.
An eighth-pallet display broadens the firm’s footprint options for retailers, and with limited downside to keeping it, management would likely wait for more market feedback.

The wooden display pallet is less aligned with the firm’s paper-based core and may be costlier to support, but after only a short time the firm would likely preserve the option until demand is clearer.
This media-focused quarter-pallet is somewhat niche, yet it remains close enough to the firm’s cardboard display competence that keeping it open is the more likely choice for now.
